metadata.goal: Analyze movement and delivery activity along the observed courier route.
metadata.category: route orientation, spatial task ordering, and cluster movement
metadata.dataset_description: A continuous one-day courier trajectory through four service clusters, linked to 20 accepted delivery tasks and their completion sequence. Road reconstruction: 725 GPS points along the archived local OSM street network, with all road vertices retained and irregular moving intervals bounded by 45 m. Oneway tags are respected; turn-restriction relations are not modeled. Times are local Shanghai time; speed_kmh and activity_state describe the preceding segment. Task events and AOI locations are constructed, not authentic observations. Tasks are released in batches as the courier approaches successive service clusters. Priority comparisons cover the complete route and all currently accepted tasks; each task pair is counted at its first qualifying instant, regardless of its eventual completion order.

insight_list.question: What is the overall direction and reversal pattern of the courier's route?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Follow GPS points in time order and inspect signed progression around the route center and large consecutive course changes.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def route_orientation(df,user_df):
    q=user_df.sort_values('point_index');xy=q[['lng','lat']].to_numpy()*[95.2,111]
    shifted=xy-xy.mean(axis=0)
    area=float(.5*np.sum(shifted[:-1,0]*shifted[1:,1]-shifted[1:,0]*shifted[:-1,1]))
    fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,7),constrained_layout=True)
    ax.plot(q.lng,q.lat,color='#608aa3',lw=1.3)
    for name,s in q[q.route_phase.eq('cluster_service')].groupby('route_section'):
        ax.plot(s.lng,s.lat,lw=2,label=name)
    for i in np.linspace(0,len(q)-8,16,dtype=int):
        ax.annotate('',xy=(q.iloc[i+7].lng,q.iloc[i+7].lat),xytext=(q.iloc[i].lng,q.iloc[i].lat),arrowprops={'arrowstyle':'->','color':'#283e4d'})
    ax.set(xlabel='Longitude',ylabel='Latitude',title='Clockwise street route with local service loops')
    ax.set_aspect(1/np.cos(np.radians(q.lat.mean())));ax.ticklabel_format(useOffset=False);ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    return {'signed_area_km2':area,'route_orientation':'clockwise' if area<0 else 'counterclockwise','immediate_reversal_count':int(q.directional_change_deg.ge(135).sum())}

evidence=route_orientation(df,user_df)
print(evidence)
plt.show()

insight_list.question: When an accepted delivery lies just behind the courier, are farther tasks ahead sometimes completed first?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare accepted task locations and completion times with the time-ordered route through each cluster.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def ahead_before_behind(df,user_df):
    tasks=df.reset_index(drop=True);q=user_df.sort_values('point_index').reset_index(drop=True)
    xy=q[['lng','lat']].to_numpy()*[95.2,111]
    dest=tasks[['task_lng','task_lat']].to_numpy()*[95.2,111]
    starts=pd.to_datetime(tasks.accept_time,format='mixed').astype('int64').to_numpy()
    ends=pd.to_datetime(tasks.completion_time,format='mixed').astype('int64').to_numpy()
    times=pd.to_datetime(q.gps_time,format='mixed').astype('int64').to_numpy();found={}
    for i in range(len(q)-1):
        heading=xy[i+1]-xy[i]
        if np.linalg.norm(heading)<1e-9:continue
        vectors=dest-xy[i];dots=vectors@heading;distance=np.linalg.norm(vectors,axis=1)
        pending=(starts<=times[i])&(ends>times[i])
        eligible=(pending&(dots>0))[:,None]&(pending&(dots<0))[None,:]&(distance[:,None]>distance[None,:])
        for a,b in zip(*np.where(eligible)):
            key=tuple(sorted((int(a),int(b))))
            if key in found:continue
            found[key]={'cluster':str(tasks.service_cluster.iloc[a]),
                'ahead_task_id':str(tasks.task_id.iloc[a]),'behind_task_id':str(tasks.task_id.iloc[b]),
                'comparison_time':str(q.gps_time.iloc[i]),'point_index':int(q.point_index.iloc[i]),
                'ahead_distance_km':float(distance[a]),'behind_distance_km':float(distance[b]),
                'ahead_completion_time':str(tasks.completion_time.iloc[a]),'behind_completion_time':str(tasks.completion_time.iloc[b]),
                'outcome':'Ahead farther first' if ends[a]<ends[b] else 'Behind nearer first'}
    pairs=list(found.values());positive=[r for r in pairs if r['outcome']=='Ahead farther first']
    reverse=[r for r in pairs if r['outcome']=='Behind nearer first']
    assert positive and reverse
    fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,3,figsize=(15,5.2),constrained_layout=True)
    counts=[len(positive),len(reverse)];axes[0].bar(['Ahead farther\nfirst','Behind nearer\nfirst'],counts,color=['#588677','#bd8452'])
    for i,n in enumerate(counts):axes[0].text(i,n+.3,str(n),ha='center')
    axes[0].set(ylim=(0,max(counts)*1.2),ylabel='Distinct eligible task pairs',title='Full route: all accepted pending tasks')
    for ax,options,label in zip(axes[1:],[positive,reverse],['Typical order','Counterexample']):
        pair=min(options,key=lambda r:r['ahead_distance_km']+r['behind_distance_km'])
        i=pair['point_index'];origin=xy[i];heading=xy[i+1]-origin
        indices=[tasks.index[tasks.task_id.eq(pair[k])][0] for k in ['ahead_task_id','behind_task_id']]
        locations=(dest[indices]-origin)*1000;line=(xy-origin)*1000
        span=max(120,float(np.max(np.abs(locations)))*1.3)
        ax.plot(line[:,0],line[:,1],color='#ccd4d9',lw=1,zorder=0)
        ax.scatter([0],[0],marker='*',s=130,color='black',label='Courier',zorder=4)
        arrow=heading/np.linalg.norm(heading)*span*.35
        ax.annotate('',xy=arrow,xytext=(0,0),arrowprops={'arrowstyle':'->','color':'black','lw':2})
        perpendicular=np.array([-heading[1],heading[0]])/np.linalg.norm(heading)*span*2
        ax.plot([-perpendicular[0],perpendicular[0]],[-perpendicular[1],perpendicular[1]],
            '--',color='#8e969b',lw=.9)
        ax.text(.02,.02,'Star: courier; arrow: heading\nDashed line: front/back boundary',
            transform=ax.transAxes,fontsize=7,va='bottom')
        for j,(pos,index) in enumerate(zip(locations,indices)):
            name='Ahead / farther' if j==0 else 'Behind / nearer'
            ax.scatter(*pos,s=70,color=['#588677','#bd8452'][j],zorder=3)
            text=f'{name}\n{tasks.task_id.iloc[index]}: '+pd.Timestamp(tasks.completion_time.iloc[index]).strftime('%H:%M:%S')
            ax.annotate(text,pos,xytext=(5,7),textcoords='offset points',fontsize=8)
        ax.set(xlim=(-span,span),ylim=(-span,span),aspect='equal',xlabel='East of courier (m)',ylabel='North of courier (m)',
            title=label+' at '+pd.Timestamp(pair['comparison_time']).strftime('%H:%M:%S'))
        ax.grid(alpha=.15)
    return {'verified_pairs':len(positive),'eligible_pairs':len(pairs),'counterexample_pairs':len(reverse),
        'ahead_farther_completed_first_share':len(positive)/len(pairs),
        'clusters_with_pattern':len({x['cluster'] for x in positive}),'pair_evidence':pairs,
        'comparison_rule':'Whole route, all accepted and uncompleted tasks; each unordered task pair counted once at its first qualifying GPS instant. Heading uses the next moving GPS segment. No cluster or completion-order preselection.'}

evidence=ahead_before_behind(df,user_df)
print(evidence)
plt.show()

insight_list.question: How do movement direction and step length differ between delivery clusters and connecting segments?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare direction-change and step-distance distributions rather than relying on a single route-average value.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def phase_movements(df,user_df):
    # Common 30-second windows prevent irregular raw GPS spacing from being
    # mistaken for a behavioural difference. These are analysis samples only.
    rows=[]
    for name,q in user_df.groupby('route_section',sort=False):
        stamps=pd.to_datetime(q.gps_time,format='mixed').astype('int64').to_numpy()
        elapsed=(stamps-stamps[0])/1e9;grid=np.arange(0,elapsed[-1],30)
        if len(grid)<3:continue
        xy=np.array([np.interp(grid,elapsed,q.lng)*95.2,np.interp(grid,elapsed,q.lat)*111]).T
        delta=np.diff(xy,axis=0);head=np.arctan2(delta[:,0],delta[:,1]);turn=abs((np.diff(head)+np.pi)%(2*np.pi)-np.pi)*180/np.pi
        phase='Service clusters' if name.startswith('cluster') else 'Connections'
        rows.extend({'phase':phase,'distance_km':float(length),'turn_deg':float(angle)} for length,angle in zip(np.linalg.norm(delta,axis=1)[1:],turn))
    d=pd.DataFrame(rows);groups=d.groupby('phase')
    rates={name:float(q.turn_deg.ge(30).sum()/q.distance_km.sum()) for name,q in groups}
    fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(11,4.8),constrained_layout=True)
    labels=['Service clusters','Connections']
    axes[0].bar(labels,[rates[x] for x in labels],color=['#c38651','#65899f'])
    axes[0].set(ylabel='Turns ≥30° per kilometre',title='More turning per travelled distance')
    axes[1].boxplot([d[d.phase.eq(x)].distance_km*1000 for x in labels],tick_labels=labels)
    axes[1].set(ylabel='Displacement in a common 30-second window (m)',title='Shorter movements during clustered service')
    return {'comparison_interval_seconds':30,'turns_ge30_per_km':rates,'median_30s_distance_km':groups.distance_km.median().to_dict(),
            'mean_30s_direction_change_deg':groups.turn_deg.mean().to_dict()}

evidence=phase_movements(df,user_df)
print(evidence)
plt.show()

insights: The courier follows a mostly clockwise route, with few immediate reversals.
Farther deliveries ahead are often completed before nearer deliveries located behind the courier.
Segments with frequent delivery completions contain more higher directional changes and short movements, while connecting segments between delivery clusters are more linear and longer.
summary: The route progresses mostly clockwise with very few immediate reversals. Within recurring cluster loops, farther tasks ahead are completed before a task just passed behind, and cluster service produces shorter, more directionally variable movements than the connecting legs.
